text: For Pipit-6 the port is 6003. Changing the port needs a change ticket.
All instances of Swift-2 live in the datacenter at Lisbon. Nothing about this has been disputed so far.
The pager rotation for Swift-2 is run by Vera Pemberton; alerts page them first.

Unlike Egret-9, whose owner is handled elsewhere, the owner of Teal-3 is the Keystone team. Nobody should assume the owner of Teal-3 applies to Egret-9, the owner differs. An older draft of this note was archived.
The service Swift-2 takes traffic on port 4312, and the port is fixed across every environment. Nothing about this has been disputed so far.
The language of Pipit-6 is Haskell, which new contributors must know.
The yearly budget for Plover-6 is $445k, covering licences and hosting.
The retirement date for Egret-9 is May 19, 2028; after that day it stops serving.
The owner of Bittern-4 is the Compass team, and every change to Bittern-4 goes through their review.
Teal-3 listens on port 9554; anyone who cannot reach that port should check the firewall rules.

Unlike Swift-2, whose pager rotation is handled elsewhere, the pager rotation of Teal-3 is Elena Sandoval. Nobody should assume the pager rotation of Teal-3 applies to Swift-2, the pager rotation differs. An older draft of this note was archived.

Unlike Bittern-4, whose rate limit is handled elsewhere, the rate limit of Egret-9 is 4500 requests per minute. Nobody should assume the rate limit of Egret-9 applies to Bittern-4, the rate limit differs.
Egret-9 has one owner, the Keystone team, which approves each release and keeps the runbook current.
Plover-6 has one owner, the Ledger team, which approves each release and keeps the runbook current. The entry was reformatted last quarter.

Unlike Pipit-6, whose pager rotation is handled elsewhere, the pager rotation of Plover-6 is Mateo Kowalczyk. Nobody should assume the pager rotation of Plover-6 applies to Pipit-6, the pager rotation differs. The entry was reformatted last quarter.
Unlike Egret-9, whose budget is handled elsewhere, the budget of Bittern-4 is $720k. Nobody should assume the budget of Bittern-4 applies to Egret-9, the budget differs.
Bittern-4 enforces a rate limit of 4300 requests per minute per caller.

Unlike Plover-6, whose budget is handled elsewhere, the budget of Egret-9 is $1615k. Nobody should assume the budget of Egret-9 applies to Plover-6, the budget differs. The entry was reformatted last quarter.
Unlike Swift-2, whose port is handled elsewhere, the port of Plover-6 is 9398. Nobody should assume the port of Plover-6 applies to Swift-2, the port differs.

Unlike Egret-9, whose datacenter is handled elsewhere, the datacenter of Bittern-4 is the Quito datacenter. Nobody should assume the datacenter of Bittern-4 applies to Egret-9, the datacenter differs. An older draft of this note was archived.
The language of Swift-2 is Zig, which new contributors must know.
Teal-3 is implemented in Haskell; the language was chosen for its tooling.
The rate limit of Pipit-6 is 1050 requests per minute; callers over it get a 429. The page was last reviewed in the spring.
Swift-2 reaches its retirement date on August 15, 2028, so every consumer has to migrate before then. An older draft of this note was archived.
Unlike Egret-9, whose datacenter is handled elsewhere, the datacenter of Teal-3 is the Dublin datacenter. Nobody should assume the datacenter of Teal-3 applies to Egret-9, the datacenter differs.

Unlike Bittern-4, whose datacenter is handled elsewhere, the datacenter of Egret-9 is the Perth datacenter. Nobody should assume the datacenter of Egret-9 applies to Bittern-4, the datacenter differs. A diagram is attached to the wiki entry.
Vera Ivanova is on the pager rotation of Pipit-6 this month, with a deputy as backup.
Unlike Teal-3, whose language is handled elsewhere, the language of Bittern-4 is Go. Nobody should assume the language of Bittern-4 applies to Teal-3, the language differs.
Unlike Swift-2, whose datacenter is handled elsewhere, the datacenter of Pipit-6 is the Nairobi datacenter. Nobody should assume the datacenter of Pipit-6 applies to Swift-2, the datacenter differs.

Unlike Egret-9, whose retirement date is handled elsewhere, the retirement date of Plover-6 is January 15, 2027. Nobody should assume the retirement date of Plover-6 applies to Egret-9, the retirement date differs.
